title: Keywords and what people click
header_line: My analysis of one book on authority and personal brand. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: What words do your customers type?

I showed a study I made for a national tourism website: the main word appeared on about 178 million pages, so reaching first place for it would be hard. I then looked at the specific searches people make.
A student said that you can use tools to type a keyword or a competitor's site and see the overlap and the words that rank, and named two tools.
I said that on the site they created a menu where people say I want to go fishing, I want to go golfing, and then they are shown pre-made itineraries. I said it is old, from about fifteen years ago.
A student said that is what she focuses on in web design: the user experience, down to what colour the buttons are and whether a button is exciting to click.

I said that there is a front end that gets a lead and a back end, once you get a lead: who picks up the phone and receives the booking. I said that the more data you have, the more you know what the visitor wanted, as when you walk into a house and see which chair they sat on.
I said that search engine optimization is a full-time job, and that you can use the tools for your own personal brand too.

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write ten words your customers type.
Write the one you could rank for.
Write what a visitor sees first.
Write who picks up the phone.

check.q: What did a student say a tool shows?
choices: The overlap and the words that rank

check.q: What did I say search engine optimization is?
What did a student say user experience includes?

recap: Know the words, the page and the back end.
